accepted_record_at_persist.in_words: Yes. The persist path reads the accepted record on every put, before anything is written. store() calls resolve_request (:151), which calls requests.get(tenant_hint, request_id) at :115. In the live composition that port is DynamoAcceptance (compose_ports :265-267), whose get() at ycharts/generate/acceptance.py:68-71 does a consistent GetItem of analysis#<request_id>#1 and returns json.loads of the record attribute (the immutable record). The store then takes only identity and owner from that dict and drops everything else, including a ticket_id member. A SEPARATE read of the same item follows at :152 (refs.get -> DynamoCommentaryRef.get, :205-211), which takes only the commentary_ref attribute. So a put does two GetItem calls on the one request item: one for the record attribute, one for the commentary_ref attribute.
members_taken: identity: read at :116; identity.request_id compared with the requested id at :118; identity.tenant_firm_id compared with the tenant hint at :119 and taken as the tenant at :121

owner: read at :117, required to be a dict at :119, owner.firm_id required equal to the tenant at :122, and the whole owner dict returned at :124 and handed to artifacts.put at :160 as the owner of the stored artifact
no other member is accessed by this module (browser_sha256, composition_ref, accepted_at, acting_principal_id, ticket_id, commentary_requested and the remaining identity members are never read here)
accepted_record_at_persist.ticket_id_reachable_in_words: Yes by code reading. A ticket_id, when the record has one, is a top-level member of the same dict that resolve_request already holds in its local variable record at :115 (acceptance.py:120-121 writes it onto the record when the public request carried one; the submission admits it only with an input_id and in the form TCK-8digits-8hex, submission.py:78-79 and AnalysisSubmissionRequest.schema.json:84-87). resolve_request returns only (tenant, owner) at :124, so it does not reach store() today; the value is in hand at :115, not behind a new read. This does not say any live record carries one.
accepted_record_at_persist.probe: In-process probe on the store's own fakes (scratch, not committed): the request record handed to requests.get was given ticket_id TCK-20261011-abcd1234 in one run and none in the other; requests.get was called once per put in both; the answer was identical in both runs and held no ticket member.

ticket_id_in_the_answer_today.when_the_record_carries_one: The answer carries nothing about the ticket. The record, with its ticket_id, is read at commentary_draft_store.py:115 and discarded at :124 (only tenant and owner leave resolve_request); the success body is the closed literal {status: OK, commentary_ref: ref} built at :171, so the first-persist answer has the same two top-level members as without a ticket id. A replay answers {status: REFUSED, reason: ALREADY_WRITTEN} at :175 and has no commentary_ref at all, so any ticket member added only to the success body would not reach a replaying caller.
ticket_id_in_the_answer_today.when_the_record_carries_none: The same: the answer carries nothing about the ticket. The same line builds the same body (:171); the store never tests for ticket_id, so there is no branch on it, no null member, and no refusal for its absence. Measured by the probe: the two answers were identical.
ticket_id_in_the_answer_today.drafter_next_step_today: Identical in both cases, because the drafter never sees a ticket id. persist_draft returns only the three ref fields (H:138). The handler then sends one commentary_ready queue message carrying {tenant, request_id} (H:324). If the run came from the analysis_ready queue (from_queue, H:296 and :325) it records stage draft_stored and stops, posting no ticket (H:325-328; module docstring H:23-26: the draft reaches the ticket only as commentary_ref). Otherwise it goes on to ticket_client.write_draft_ticket(draft, item[ticket_context]) at H:329, which POSTs a NEW ticket to /api/scoped/tickets (ticket_client.py:9, :70) with report_request_id from the composition (entry.py:210), not a ticket id: ticket_context holds no ticket_id key (entry.py:209-220) and no file under data/transcripts/scripts/commentary reads one (ticket_id there appears only in the response handling at ticket_client.py:72 and the output at H:333; the docstring at entry.py:266 says a consumer reads ticket_id from the records, but no code does). On a replay the persist call raises DRAFT_STORE_ALREADY_WRITTEN (H:124) and the record lands in failed (H:334-336).
